tagline: A mountain village above the Las Vegas valley.
intro: From Mount Charleston, Kyle Canyon Road runs down toward Lower Kyle Canyon, leaving a village set in the Spring Mountains at about 7,500 feet. Las Vegas sits near 2,000 feet, and the mean high up here runs about 20 degrees cooler, which is why Las Vegans come up to vacation.

Around 1870 to 1880, Conrad Keil, also known as Kyle, built a sawmill and cabin in the canyon. Edmund Griffith started a campground about 1905, and his Charleston Park Lodge stood where the village library and volunteer fire department are now.

moments.title: Mount Charleston
moments.text: The village fills a valley of the Spring Mountains noted for its hiking trails, where, unlike the rest of arid Nevada, enough rain and snow fall to keep a coniferous forest.

moments.title: Tule Springs
moments.text: Spring-fed lakes make an oasis in the Mojave at an old guest ranch where out-of-state residents once came to live in Nevada for its easy divorce; several buildings remain, and a few peacocks.
